To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the leading-twist transversity distribution does no not contribute to hard electroproduction of vector mesons, and that the helicity selection rules for hard electroproduction are correct to all orders of pQCD.

the leading-twist contribution to the hard scattering coefficient for the exclusive electroproduction of a vector meson vanishes, that this is true to all orders of QCD perturbation theory, and that the vanishing of the hard scattering coefficient is a consequence of the helicity and chirality selection rules of QCD.
The leading-twist hard scattering coefficient for exclusive electroproduction of a transversively polarized vector mesons V vanishes to any order in perturbation theory.
